key_insight: LLM-based analysis of Taiwanese online health discussions found patient-expressed frictions in 83.1% of confirmed forum articles, most commonly information gaps and emotional burden.
clinical_relevance: The findings may inform patient-centered communication and support priorities; this study did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or treatment outcomes.
method: Applied an eight-domain, Taiwan-contextualized friction framework to Traditional Chinese health discussions.
Used an LLM to assess relevance, patient or family authorship, and expressed needs across 10,130 distinct sampled units.
Checked results against a second vendor, two physicians’ independent labels, and a keyword pipeline.
evidence_signal: Among 2,395 model-confirmed forum articles, 59.5% expressed information gaps and 39.0% emotional burden; physician review covered 160 accepted and rejected units.
watch_item: Online, pipeline-seeded samples may not represent all patients, and some findings were instrument-dependent; the supplied abstract is truncated.
paper_title: Patient-Expressed Needs, Burdens and Barriers in Taiwanese Online Health Discussions: A Taiwan-Contextualized Friction Framework Applied With Large Language Model-Based Social Listening
